grades: Juniors or seniors (the page intro says current and rising seniors)
duration: 6 weeks, 8am to 5pm Monday to Wednesday, employer days Thursday and Friday
pay_detail: $2,000 stipend and 6 hours of college credit. Tools and materials provided.
name: Careers Electric High School Summer Academy
org: Wake Tech Community College with Wake County Public School System
what_you_do: A six-week summer academy. Classes are Monday to Wednesday at the Wake Tech Southern Wake Campus. On Thursday and Friday you train on the job with a local electrical employer.
who_can_apply: Wake County high school juniors or seniors who are allowed to work in the U.S. You must have applied for Career and College Promise at Wake Tech. The path is Electrical Systems Technology.
deadline_text: The 2026 application window has closed. Check back for information on the 2027 Summer Academy. The page lists no 2027 dates.
how_to_apply: Talk with the career coordinator at your school. Or talk with Career and Technical Education staff. You can also email Todd Campbell. He runs the Wake Tech Electrification Training Project.
notes: You need your own transportation to Wake Tech and to the employer, though help may be available. Attend at least 90% of sessions. The 2026 page listed juniors and seniors expected to graduate in 2026 or 2027.
